newsitem.title: CANADA: REPAP says many suitors in due diligence.
newsitem.headline: REPAP says many suitors in due diligence.

text.p: Repap Enterprises Inc said on Wednesday that about 10 companies are in the due diligence process regarding a buyout of the forest products company.

Daniel Veniez, Repap's vice president of corporate affairs, told Reuters that "close to" 10 companies, including Canadian, American and European concerns, are participating in a due diligence process.
A number of the companies have already been in Repap's data room and toured some of the company's facilities in Canada and the United States, but the process is ongoing, he said.
"These folks have invested in a process that has lasted a couple of months and will probably go for another few months," Veniez said.

He declined to divulge the name of the companies inspecting Repap's books and operations, but speculation in the financial community is that they include Toronto-based Abitibi-Price Inc, UPM-Kymmene Oy of Finland, Stora AB of Sweden and several U.S. companies -- Champion International Corp, International Paper Co, Consolidated Papers Inc and Weyerhaeuser Co.
"After they have gone through their due diligence, they will come back to our investment bankers with offers," Veniez said.
Repap indicated in July that it had hired New York investment banker Dillon, Read & Co to seek strategic alternatives for the company, including an outright sale.

Veniez said Repap is seeking to sell the company in its entirety, and would not consider selling its coated paper operations in New Brunswick and Wisconsin, or its pulp facilities in British Columbia, individually.
Veniez said Repap chairman and chief executive George Petty and Stephen Larson president and chief operating officer, are both involved in the due diligence process.
On the Toronto Stock Exchange at midday Wednesday, Repap common shares were trading at 5.60, up 0.60 from Tuesday.
